text: In the standard linear model assumed by Western philosophy and classical physics, temporal positions are ordered so as to be isomorphic to which mathematical structure?
choices: The real number line — a single total order that is transitive, asymmetric, irreflexive, and contains no loops
A circle (the 1-sphere S¹), so that traveling far enough toward the future brings you back to the past
A branching tree with a unique past but multiple possible future continuations
The integers, in which every moment has an immediate successor and an immediate predecessor
explanation: The linear model treats time as isomorphic to the real number line: one loopless, total ordering. The circle (option 1) is circular time and the tree (option 2) is branching time — both rival topologies — while the integers (option 3) describe a discrete order-type, a separate question about local structure rather than the standard linear picture.
